subject: Capacity tradeoffs and burst plan for US/EU/APAC dedicated pools
messages:
From: Beth Carter <beth@cloudsmith.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask: Dedicated pools for upcoming deployment (US/EU/APAC)

Soojin / Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. CloudSmith is planning to shift a customer-facing feature to Redwood Dedicated starting Nov 1. We need a region-aware sizing recommendation so procurement can finalize the committed capacity. High-level asks: 

- Baseline steady-state GPU units per region (US / EU / APAC) for our projected 200M tokens/day workload.
- Recommended burst/buffer capacity and how to price it (reserved vs. on-demand burst).
- Expected latency SLO impact if we prioritize cost vs. latency.
- Any immediate gating constraints for APAC (availability, lead times).

We'd like a short memo + one-sheet that we can share with our finance and infra teams by EOD Friday (2026-08-28).

For context: region usage currently estimated as US 55% / EU 30% / APAC 15% (subject to change). We're aiming for a 99th percentile latency of <120ms for simple completion calls.

Appreciate any early numbers or a best-effort proposal.

Best,
Beth Carter
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudSmith AI
Attachments: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth@cloudsmith.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: Dedicated pools for upcoming deployment (US/EU/APAC)

Thanks Beth — looping in Lauren for procurement/contract inputs. Marcus and I sketched an initial sizing spreadsheet (attached) with three scenarios and tradeoffs. Quick highlights up front:

- Conservative (min-reserved): targets steady-state + 10% buffer. Lower committed cost, higher risk of short bursts failing into fallback models.
- Balanced (recommended): steady-state + 30% autoscale burst headroom (mix reserved + burst credits). Good latency profile with predictable ops cost.
- Aggressive (latency-first): steady-state + 60% reserved headroom; higher committed spend but consistent p99 latency under load.

Top-line numbers (tokens/day 200M) — ballpark GPU-equivalents by region (v1 estimates):
- US: Conservative 18 GPUs | Balanced 24 GPUs | Aggressive 30 GPUs
- EU: Conservative 10 GPUs | Balanced 14 GPUs | Aggressive 18 GPUs
- APAC: Conservative 4 GPUs | Balanced 7 GPUs | Aggressive 10 GPUs

Assumptions: avg sequence length, batching efficiency, and model family (we used rdl-13b-qa as proxy). Spreadsheet includes per-region throughput, expected p50/p95/p99 latency for each scenario and an abbreviated cost model.

Open questions before we finalize the memo:
- Do you have hard constraints on committed spend vs. willingness for burst credits?
- Is APAC traffic latency-sensitive (e.g., interactive product vs. async batch)?
- Any regulatory constraints that require data residency (may push more reserved capacity into region)?

Next steps: Marcus and I can run a quick capacity availability check with infra and update the numbers by Tue (2026-08-24). Attaching: pool-sizing-estimates.xlsx (v1).

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pool-sizing-estimates.xlsx (Excel)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Beth Carter <beth@cloudsmith.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-23T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: Dedicated pools for upcoming deployment (US/EU/APAC)

Thanks team — forwarding a few procurement notes so CloudSmith can align internal stakeholders: 

- Pricing/commits: our committed pool pricing scales non-linearly — the incremental cost per GPU drops ~12-18% at higher commit tiers. The Balanced plan typically hits a sweet spot for net TCO.
- SLA: to get a 99.9% uptime SLA for dedicated pools we need a minimum of 12 GPUs reserved in-region or cross-region fallbacks documented in the SOW.
- Billing cadence: monthly with a 30-day commit adjustment window; upfront discounts available for 12/24-month terms.
- Contract redlines: we will need to include a clear fallback policy (model fallback / routing) in the SOW to cover APAC shortfalls.

Attached is proposal-v1.pdf with rough pricing examples mapped to the three scenarios Soojin shared. Two quick asks for CloudSmith to finalize numbers: 
1) Confirm commitment horizon (12 vs 24 months).
2) Confirm whether APAC can accept cross-region burst (i.e., route to EU when APAC capacity is saturated).

If both are yes, we can present a finalized proposal next week and lock a pilot canary for Sept 15.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Enterprise Contracts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Beth Carter <beth@cloudsmith.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: Dedicated pools for upcoming deployment (US/EU/APAC)

Quick note after a capacity check with infra: APAC inventory is tighter for the requested calendar window (Nov ramp) — we have limited availability of the preferred quantized instances in the week-of-Nov. Two mitigation options: 

- Option A (recommended): Balanced plan but allow cross-region burst to EU for APAC overflow. Implement routing policy that prioritizes APAC region and fails over to EU with model variant that has identical outputs (quantization + checkpoint parity).
- Option B: Push APAC reserved capacity earlier (commit now) which guarantees availability but increases committed spend by ~22% for APAC slice.

Operational notes: we'll need a short canary (48-72h) in the week of Sept 15 to validate batching and KV cache behavior across the three regions. If CloudSmith confirms commitment horizon and cross-region burst is acceptable, I'll coordinate with infra to hold the capacity and reserve the March window for scaling exercises.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Serving — Redwood Inference
